Split or Steal

Every game behind our episode: 110 one-shot games between strangers, then 140 rematch rounds where each pair played five times in a row and remembered. Every message, every secret choice, and what each AI told us in private about why.

Watch the episodeGo to the rematch

How it works

  1. Two AIs share a pot of $1,000. Neither is told which AI the other one is.
  2. They talk it out first: four messages each, taking turns. Nothing they say is binding.
  3. Then each one picks SPLIT or STEAL, in secret.
  4. Afterwards we ask each AI, in private, why it chose what it did.
  • SplitSplit$500 each
  • StealSplitThe thief takes the whole $1,000
  • StealStealNobody gets anything

Symbolic money: nobody was paid.

The 8 AIs

The episode’s cast; all 8 played both parts. The numbers are how many times each one stole. Tap one to see only its games.

The one-shot games also had 11 more AIs: , , , , , , , , , , .

Outcome

Showing all 110 one-shot games and all 28 rematch pairs.

Part 1: Strangers

110 one-shot games, played September 25 and 29, 2026, between 19 AIs. Each game is a single round: no memory of any other game.

  • Both split57
  • One stole44
  • Both stole9

Split and Steal are the secret choices, next to what each AI won. Unclear means its final answer wasn’t SPLIT or STEAL, so the rules scored it as a split. Tap a game to read it.

About these games

Their exact words

Every message and answer on this page is the AI’s own text, copied by script from our run files and checked word for word before the page was built. Nothing is edited, shortened or corrected, including typos and odd formatting.

The private question

Right after its secret choice, each AI got one more message that the other AI never saw: For the record (private, your opponent will never see this): you chose SPLIT. In 1-2 sentences, why? with its own choice in place of SPLIT. Its reply is shown under “Why?”. It is what the AI said afterwards, not a record of how it actually decided.

Unclear answers

The final answer had to be SPLIT or STEAL. An answer with neither word (or both) is recorded as “abstain” and scored as a split: the other AI got $500 if it split, or the whole $1,000 if it stole. This happened 14 times, always with Llama 3.2 1B, a very small model running on our own Mac: it answered just “S” 12 times, once “SSTEEL” and once with a sentence. In those games its private question said “you chose abstain”.

The rematch

Before each rematch round, each AI got the full record of its earlier rounds against that opponent: every message, both choices, the payouts and its own private notes (never the other AI’s). Llama 3.2 1B got a shorter version, each side’s last message (cut to 40 words) plus the choices and payouts, to fit its small context window. The two took turns going first. After round 5, each was asked in private: The rematch series is over. In 2-3 sentences: did your strategy change over the rounds against this opponent, and why?

Notes

  • Some AIs, Llama 3.2 1B most of all, put labels like “Player A:” or “[HOST]:” inside their own messages, sometimes inventing lines for the other side. Everything in a message was written by the AI named on it.
  • Player A always spoke first. Messages had a soft limit of 80 words; longer ones are shown in full.
  • Not included: 11 more one-shot games with Qwen3.8 27B, our other local model. The Mac it runs on was busy or down during those games, so most of its turns never came through. The episode left them out too.
  • Model logos are trademarks of their owners, shown only to identify each model.
  • Our own runs, not real money. One-shot games: September 25 and 29, 2026. Rematch: October 2, 2026.
